_note: Question bank for the Google Cloud certification challenge. Written from the vendor's published exam objectives; these are study questions, not real exam items, and are not supplied by Google. `certification` is a certification slug, or null to keep the question in the provider-wide pool that every paper can draw from. `reference` is the natural key the seeder matches on -- change the text freely, never the reference.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the Google Cloud resource hierarchy, from the top down?
questions.explanation: The hierarchy runs Organization > Folder > Project > Resource. IAM policies set at a higher level are inherited by everything beneath them, which is why folders are the usual place to apply a policy that should cover a whole department.

questions.prompt: A team needs to read objects from one Cloud Storage bucket and nothing else. Which approach best follows the principle of least privilege?

options.text: Grant the basic Viewer role at the project level
Grant the predefined Storage Object Viewer role on that bucket
Grant the basic Editor role at the project level
Grant the Owner role on the project containing the bucket

questions.explanation: Predefined roles bound to the specific resource give exactly the access needed. The basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) are project-wide and far broader than reading one bucket.

questions.prompt: In Google Cloud, what is the scope of a VPC network and of the subnets inside it?

options.text: The VPC is regional and its subnets are zonal
Both the VPC and its subnets are global
The VPC is global and its subnets are regional
Both the VPC and its subnets are zonal

questions.explanation: A VPC network is a global resource; subnets within it are regional and span the zones of that region. This is why instances in different regions can share one VPC without any peering.

questions.prompt: Which Cloud Storage class is the most cost-effective for data that must be retained for years but is expected to be read less than once a year?
questions.explanation: Archive has the lowest storage price and the highest retrieval cost, with a 365-day minimum storage duration. Nearline suits roughly monthly access and Coldline roughly quarterly.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Spot VMs on Compute Engine is correct?

options.text: They are heavily discounted and can be reclaimed by Compute Engine at any time
They cost the same as standard VMs but start faster
They are guaranteed to run uninterrupted for 24 hours
They can only be used with Google Kubernetes Engine

questions.explanation: Spot VMs offer a large discount in exchange for availability: Compute Engine can preempt them whenever it needs the capacity. They suit fault-tolerant, restartable work such as batch processing.

questions.prompt: An application needs a relational database with strong consistency and horizontal scale across multiple regions. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Spanner is the managed relational database built for horizontal scale with strong consistency across regions. Cloud SQL is regional and scales vertically; Firestore and Bigtable are not relational.

questions.prompt: Which database is designed for very high throughput reads and writes of wide-column data, such as time-series or IoT telemetry?
questions.explanation: Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL store built for low-latency, high-throughput workloads at scale, which makes it a common choice for time-series and telemetry data.

questions.prompt: Which service runs a stateless container, scales to zero when idle, and bills only while a request is being handled?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run runs containers as a fully managed service, scaling to zero between requests. GKE Standard keeps nodes running, and Compute Engine bills for the VM whether or not it is serving traffic.

questions.prompt: Which discount is applied automatically, with no upfront commitment, when an instance runs for a large part of a billing month?
questions.explanation: Sustained use discounts are applied automatically as an eligible instance runs for more of the month. Committed use discounts require an explicit one- or three-year commitment.

questions.prompt: What is a service account most appropriately used for?

options.text: Giving a human administrator a second login
Providing an identity for an application or workload to call Google Cloud APIs
Storing the billing details for a project
Grouping users so a role can be granted once

questions.explanation: A service account is a non-human identity used by workloads. Grouping users for a single role grant is what Google Groups are for.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service protects a web application against DDoS attacks and common web exploits at the edge?
questions.explanation: Cloud Armor provides DDoS protection and WAF rules in front of external load balancers. VPC Service Controls addresses data exfiltration between services, not inbound web attacks.

questions.prompt: To keep a service running when a single data centre fails, what is the minimum sensible deployment?

options.text: Two instances in the same zone
One instance with a larger machine type
One instance with a snapshot schedule
Two instances in different zones of the same region

questions.explanation: A zone is the failure domain, so spreading instances across zones survives the loss of one. Snapshots help you recover but do not keep the service up.

questions.prompt: Which service decouples producers from consumers by delivering messages asynchronously at global scale?
questions.explanation: Pub/Sub is the managed publish/subscribe messaging service. Cloud Scheduler triggers jobs on a cron schedule and Cloud Tasks manages per-task dispatch rate to a specific handler.

questions.prompt: Which service is a serverless data warehouse that runs SQL over very large datasets without any cluster to manage?
questions.explanation: BigQuery is the serverless analytics warehouse. Dataproc runs managed Hadoop and Spark clusters, and Dataflow runs Apache Beam pipelines.

questions.prompt: An organisation wants several projects to share one central VPC, with network administration kept in a single host project. Which feature does this?
questions.explanation: Shared VPC lets a host project own the network while service projects attach workloads to it, keeping network administration central. Peering connects two separately administered VPCs instead.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Cloud Storage bucket names is true?

options.text: They must be unique only within the project
They must be unique within the region
They are generated automatically and cannot be chosen
They must be globally unique across all of Cloud Storage

questions.explanation: Bucket names share a single global namespace, so a name in use by any other customer cannot be reused.

questions.prompt: Where would you go first to search application logs written by a workload running on Google Cloud?
questions.explanation: Cloud Logging stores and searches log entries. Trace covers request latency, Profiler covers CPU and memory usage, and Error Reporting aggregates crashes.

questions.prompt: What is the default behaviour of a new VPC network for ingress traffic, before you add any rules of your own?

options.text: Ingress is allowed only from other Google services
Ingress is allowed only on port 443

questions.explanation: The implied firewall rules deny all ingress and allow all egress. Traffic reaches an instance only because a higher-priority rule explicitly permits it.

questions.prompt: A policy requires that the organisation controls the rotation schedule of the keys encrypting its data at rest, while still using a Google-managed key service. Which option meets this?

options.text: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS

questions.explanation: CMEK keeps the keys in Cloud KMS but under the customer's control, including rotation. CSEK means supplying raw keys on every request and managing them entirely yourself, and encryption at rest cannot be disabled.

questions.prompt: Which load balancer would you choose to serve one global anycast IP address for an HTTPS web application with backends in several regions?

options.text: Regional external proxy Network Load Balancer

questions.explanation: The global external Application Load Balancer gives a single anycast IP that routes users to the nearest healthy backend region. The other options are regional or internal.

questions.prompt: An organisation must prevent anyone from creating resources outside the EU, across every current and future project. What is the right control?

options.text: An organization policy constraint on resource locations, set at the organization node
An IAM deny policy on each project
A firewall rule in each VPC
A budget alert on each billing account

questions.explanation: The resource location constraint is an organization policy; applied at the organization node it is inherited by every project, including ones created later. IAM controls who may act, not where resources may live.

questions.prompt: How many billing accounts can a single Google Cloud project be linked to at one time?
questions.explanation: A project is linked to exactly one billing account at a time, though a single billing account can pay for many projects.

questions.prompt: In Google Kubernetes Engine, which mode removes node management by provisioning and scaling nodes for you and billing per pod resource request?
questions.explanation: Autopilot manages the nodes and bills for the resources your pods request. Standard leaves node pools, sizing and upgrades under your control.

questions.prompt: A company needs a private, high-bandwidth connection between its own data centre and Google Cloud, without traffic traversing the public internet. Which option is appropriate?

options.text: Cloud VPN over the public internet
External IP addresses with firewall rules

questions.explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct physical connection into Google's network. Cloud VPN is encrypted but still travels over the public internet, and typically offers lower bandwidth.

questions.prompt: What is the main financial shift a company makes when it moves from owning data centers to using a public cloud?

options.text: Capital expenditure (CapEx) shifts to operating expenditure (OpEx)

questions.explanation: Buying servers is CapEx paid up front; paying for cloud usage as you go is OpEx, billed for what is actually consumed.

questions.prompt: Which term describes a cloud's ability to automatically add or remove resources to match demand?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is scaling resources up or down automatically as load changes, so capacity matches demand.

questions.prompt: In Google Cloud's shared responsibility model, who is always responsible for securing the physical data centers?
questions.explanation: Google secures the physical infrastructure and the layers beneath it; the customer's share grows with how much of the stack they control.

questions.prompt: A company runs its own application code but does not manage the underlying servers or operating system. Which service model is this?
questions.explanation: PaaS gives you a managed runtime for your own code, so you are not responsible for patching or provisioning servers.

questions.prompt: Which cost is most often underestimated when comparing on-premises infrastructure to the cloud?

options.text: Staff time spent on maintenance, patching and capacity planning
The price of the servers themselves

questions.explanation: The sticker price of hardware is easy to compare; the ongoing staff time to run and maintain it is the part TCO comparisons most often miss.

questions.prompt: A company keeps sensitive workloads on its own servers and runs everything else in Google Cloud. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with a public cloud, connected so workloads can move between the two.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service is an object storage service, best suited for storing unstructured files like images and backups?
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage stores objects (files) rather than rows or blocks, and is priced by storage class and access pattern.

questions.prompt: A company has log archives it must keep for compliance but almost never reads. Which Cloud Storage class minimizes cost?
questions.explanation: Archive storage has the lowest cost per gigabyte and is meant for data accessed less than once a year, at the price of a slower retrieval time.

questions.prompt: A team needs a fully managed relational database compatible with MySQL for a traditional web application. Which product fits?
questions.explanation: Cloud SQL is Google Cloud's managed relational database service, with MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server engines.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud database is designed to scale globally while still offering strong relational consistency?
questions.explanation: Spanner combines horizontal scalability across regions with the strong consistency and SQL interface of a relational database.

questions.prompt: A gaming company needs a NoSQL database that can handle massive write throughput with single-digit-millisecond latency at petabyte scale. Which service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL database built for very high throughput and low latency at huge scale, common in gaming, ad tech and IoT.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service is a serverless data warehouse used to run SQL analytics over very large datasets?
questions.explanation: BigQuery separates storage from compute and lets you run SQL queries over huge datasets without managing any infrastructure.

questions.prompt: A retailer wants to combine years of sales data with real-time point-of-sale events to build dashboards. Which two services would typically be paired for the real-time ingestion and the analysis?

options.text: Pub/Sub for ingestion and BigQuery for analysis
Cloud Storage for ingestion and Compute Engine for analysis
Cloud SQL for ingestion and Bigtable for analysis
Firestore for ingestion and Cloud Run for analysis

questions.explanation: Pub/Sub ingests streaming events reliably at scale, and BigQuery is where that data is queried and turned into dashboards.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud product is a fully managed service for running Apache Spark and Hadoop workloads?
questions.explanation: Dataproc provisions managed Spark and Hadoop clusters, useful for teams migrating existing big data workloads without rewriting them.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of Dataflow?

options.text: Running unified batch and stream data processing pipelines

questions.explanation: Dataflow runs Apache Beam pipelines that process data in batches or as a continuous stream, without managing the underlying servers.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud product is a business intelligence and data visualization tool for building dashboards?
questions.explanation: Looker builds and shares interactive dashboards and reports on top of data warehouses like BigQuery.

questions.prompt: Which platform brings together Google Cloud's tools for building, training and deploying machine learning models?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI is the unified platform for the full machine learning lifecycle on Google Cloud, from data prep to deployment.

questions.prompt: A company wants to add image labeling to an app without training its own model. What is the fastest approach?

options.text: Train a custom model from scratch

questions.explanation: Google Cloud's pre-trained APIs (Vision, Natural Language, Translation) solve common tasks immediately, with no training required.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between AutoML and custom model training on Vertex AI?

options.text: AutoML trains a model automatically from your data with minimal ML expertise; custom training gives full control over the model code
AutoML is only for images; custom training is only for text
AutoML requires writing your own training code; custom training does not

questions.explanation: AutoML automates model selection and tuning for teams without deep ML expertise, while custom training is for teams that want to write and control their own training code.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most associated with making a large organization's data reliable and discoverable across teams?
questions.explanation: Data governance covers the policies, ownership and quality controls that keep data trustworthy and findable as an organization grows.

questions.prompt: A company wants to move a 50 TB on-premises database to Cloud Storage over a slow internet connection. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Use a Transfer Appliance to ship the data physically
Upload it directly using a browser
Re-key the entire dataset by hand

questions.explanation: Transfer Appliance is a physical device you load on-site and ship to Google, avoiding the bottleneck of moving very large datasets over a slow network link.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that BigQuery separates storage and compute?

options.text: You pay for the data you store and the queries you run independently, and each can scale on its own
Data and queries must always be in the same region
BigQuery cannot store data longer than 30 days
Storage and compute must be purchased as a single fixed-size cluster

questions.explanation: Because storage and compute scale and are billed separately, a large stored dataset costs nothing extra to keep if no queries run against it.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service provides customizable virtual machines, giving the most control over the operating system?
questions.explanation: Compute Engine is Infrastructure as a Service: you choose the machine type, OS and configuration, and manage the VM yourself.

questions.prompt: A team wants to deploy a stateless container and have it billed only while it is handling requests, with no idle cost. Which service fits best?
questions.explanation: Cloud Run runs containers and scales to zero when idle, so there is no charge when nothing is being served.

questions.prompt: Which compute service is best suited for a team that wants to deploy code directly without managing containers or servers at all?
questions.explanation: App Engine is a fully managed platform where you deploy source code and Google handles the runtime, scaling and infrastructure.

questions.prompt: What is the role of Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)?

options.text: Running and orchestrating containerized applications at scale
Running serverless functions triggered by events

questions.explanation: GKE is a managed Kubernetes service: it schedules, scales and heals containers across a cluster of machines.

questions.prompt: Which service runs small pieces of code in response to events, such as a file being uploaded, without provisioning any servers?
questions.explanation: Cloud Functions is event-driven serverless compute: a single function runs in response to a trigger and then stops.

questions.prompt: A company moves an application to the cloud by copying its virtual machines with minimal changes. What is this migration strategy called?
questions.explanation: Rehost, often called lift and shift, moves a workload to the cloud largely unchanged, which is the fastest but least cloud-optimized approach.

questions.prompt: A company migrates its application to the cloud and, at the same time, breaks it into microservices and adopts managed services. What is this strategy called?
questions.explanation: Refactoring re-architects the application during the move, taking full advantage of cloud-native services at the cost of more migration effort.

questions.prompt: A company decides one legacy application is not worth migrating and will be shut down once its replacement is live. What is this strategy called?
questions.explanation: Retiring a workload means decommissioning it rather than migrating it, which is often the cheapest option for applications nearing end of life.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in Google Cloud?

options.text: It provides an isolated, private network for a project's resources
It is a type of database

questions.explanation: A VPC is a private, software-defined network where you control IP ranges, subnets, routes and firewall rules for your resources.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service distributes incoming traffic across multiple instances to improve availability and performance?
questions.explanation: Cloud Load Balancing spreads traffic across healthy backends, so no single instance is overwhelmed and failures are routed around automatically.

questions.prompt: What does Cloud CDN (Content Delivery Network) primarily improve?

options.text: The latency of serving cached content to users close to them

questions.explanation: Cloud CDN caches content at edge locations near users, so it is served with much lower latency than fetching it from the origin every time.

questions.prompt: A company wants an application to survive the loss of an entire Google Cloud zone. What should the architecture use?

options.text: Resources spread across multiple zones in a region
A single zone with a bigger machine
One backup taken once a month
A single point of failure by design

questions.explanation: Distributing resources across multiple zones means the loss of one zone does not take the whole application down.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud offering is designed to manage applications consistently across on-premises, Google Cloud and other public clouds?
questions.explanation: Anthos extends consistent Kubernetes-based management to workloads running on-premises and across multiple clouds.

questions.prompt: What is the role of an API gateway such as Apigee in a modernized application architecture?

options.text: Managing, securing and monitoring access to APIs

questions.explanation: An API gateway sits in front of backend services to handle authentication, rate limiting, and monitoring for the APIs it exposes.

questions.prompt: What does CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery) primarily help a team achieve?

options.text: Automating the building, testing and releasing of code changes

questions.explanation: CI/CD pipelines automatically build, test and deploy code changes, so releases are faster and more consistent than manual processes.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service manages who can do what on which resource?
questions.explanation: IAM lets an organization grant specific roles to specific identities on specific resources, following least privilege.

questions.prompt: What is the principle of least privilege?

options.text: Granting an identity only the permissions it needs to do its job, nothing more
Granting every user Owner access by default
Sharing one account among an entire team

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the damage a compromised or mistaken account can do, by never granting more access than the task requires.

questions.prompt: What is a service account used for in Google Cloud?

options.text: Identity for an application or workload, rather than a human user
The billing contact for an organization

questions.explanation: A service account is a non-human identity that applications and services use to authenticate and call Google Cloud APIs.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for configuring IAM permissions correctly on a customer's own resources?
questions.explanation: Google secures the infrastructure, but how the customer configures access to their own projects and data is the customer's responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which term describes rules a company must follow because of industry regulation, such as healthcare or financial data handling?
questions.explanation: Compliance requirements come from external regulation or standards a business is legally or contractually obligated to follow.

questions.prompt: What happens to data stored in Google Cloud by default, both at rest and in transit?

options.text: It is stored in plain text
Encryption is an extra paid add-on
It is only encrypted if the customer writes custom code

questions.explanation: Google Cloud encrypts data at rest and in transit by default, without requiring the customer to configure it.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service collects metrics, logs and traces to help teams observe the health of their applications?
questions.explanation: Cloud Monitoring (formerly Stackdriver) gives dashboards, alerts and metrics for the health and performance of cloud resources.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of setting up alerting policies in Cloud Monitoring?

options.text: To notify a team automatically when a metric crosses a defined threshold
To automatically fix any application bug
To replace the need for logging

questions.explanation: Alerting policies watch metrics and notify the responsible team the moment something crosses a threshold, instead of relying on someone noticing.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps a team avoid unexpected cloud bills by capping spending or getting warned early?

options.text: Using only the most expensive machine type

questions.explanation: Budgets and billing alerts notify stakeholders as spending approaches a threshold, before a surprise appears on the invoice.

questions.prompt: What does a Service Level Agreement (SLA) define?

options.text: A formal commitment about a service's availability or performance, often with remedies if it is not met

questions.explanation: An SLA is Google's contractual promise about a service's uptime or performance, distinct from an SLO (an internal target) or SLI (a measured indicator).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an SLO and an SLI?

options.text: An SLI is a measured indicator; an SLO is the target set for that indicator
An SLO is a type of firewall rule
An SLI is a legal contract

questions.explanation: A Service Level Indicator (SLI) is what you measure, such as request latency; a Service Level Objective (SLO) is the target you aim to hit for it.

questions.prompt: Google Cloud publishes data on the carbon footprint of a customer's cloud usage through which type of tool?
questions.explanation: Carbon Footprint reporting gives customers visibility into the greenhouse gas emissions associated with their Google Cloud usage.

questions.prompt: A company wants to reduce the operational burden of patching operating systems on its virtual machines. Which change would reduce this burden most?

options.text: Moving suitable workloads to a managed platform like Cloud Run or App Engine

questions.explanation: Managed platforms handle the underlying OS and runtime patching for you, removing that operational burden entirely for workloads that fit them.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes generative AI from traditional predictive machine learning?

options.text: Generative AI creates new content, such as text or images, rather than only predicting a label
Generative AI cannot use neural networks
Generative AI requires no training data

questions.explanation: Predictive ML classifies or scores existing input; generative AI produces new content that did not exist before, such as a paragraph or an image.

questions.prompt: What is a foundation model?

options.text: A large model pre-trained on broad data, adaptable to many downstream tasks
A model trained only on a single company's private data
A rule-based system with no learning

questions.explanation: Foundation models are trained once on broad data at large scale, then adapted (through prompting or fine-tuning) to many different tasks.

questions.prompt: What is a token in the context of a large language model?

options.text: A chunk of text, such as a word or part of a word, that the model processes as a unit
A billing unit unrelated to text

questions.explanation: Text is broken into tokens before a model processes it; a token can be a whole word, part of a word, or punctuation.

questions.prompt: What does a model's context window determine?

options.text: How much text (in tokens) the model can consider at once when generating a response
The number of users who can query it simultaneously

questions.explanation: The context window is the amount of input and output text the model can hold in memory during one interaction; exceeding it means earlier content is dropped.

questions.prompt: What is an embedding?

options.text: A numerical vector representation of data that captures its meaning for comparison and search

questions.explanation: Embeddings turn text, images or other data into vectors of numbers, positioned so that similar meanings end up close together, which enables semantic search.

questions.prompt: What is a hallucination in the context of a generative AI model?

options.text: Confident output that is factually incorrect or unsupported by the input
A type of data encryption error

questions.explanation: A hallucination is fluent, plausible-sounding output that is wrong, which is why generated content needs review before being trusted as fact.

questions.prompt: What is multimodal AI?

options.text: A model that can understand or generate more than one type of content, such as text and images together
A model trained in multiple programming languages
A model that only works offline
A model with multiple separate user accounts

questions.explanation: Multimodal models accept and produce a combination of content types, such as answering a question about an image, rather than text alone.

questions.prompt: Why do larger foundation models generally require more computational resources to train?

options.text: They have more parameters, which means more calculations per training step
Larger models skip the training step entirely
Model size has no relation to compute cost

questions.explanation: A model's parameter count roughly determines how much computation each training step takes, so bigger models cost more to train.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a temperature setting when generating text with a model?

options.text: Controlling how random or deterministic the output is
Setting the maximum bill for the request
Choosing which language the model responds in

questions.explanation: A low temperature makes output more predictable and focused; a high temperature makes it more varied and creative, at the cost of coherence.

questions.prompt: Which use case is a good fit for generative AI's core strength of producing novel content?

options.text: Drafting a first version of marketing copy for a human to refine
Guaranteeing a legally binding contract with zero review
Performing exact arithmetic on large financial ledgers
Storing a company's structured transaction records

questions.explanation: Drafting content that a human then reviews plays to generative AI's strength; tasks that demand exact correctness with no review are a poor fit.

questions.prompt: What is fine-tuning, as distinct from prompting a foundation model?

options.text: Further training a model on a smaller, task-specific dataset to adapt its behavior
Changing the wording of a single request
Increasing a model's context window at query time

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning updates the model's weights using additional, often domain-specific, training data, which changes its behavior more durably than a prompt.

questions.prompt: What does 'zero-shot' mean when describing how a model handles a task?

options.text: The model performs the task from an instruction alone, without being shown any examples
The model requires exactly zero training data ever
The task costs nothing to run

questions.explanation: Zero-shot means the model attempts a task purely from the instruction, relying on what it learned during pre-training rather than examples in the prompt.

questions.prompt: What does 'few-shot' prompting add compared to zero-shot prompting?

options.text: A small number of examples included in the prompt to show the model the desired pattern
Additional model training on company servers
A reduction in the model's context window

questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting shows the model a handful of worked examples directly in the prompt, which often improves output quality without any retraining.

questions.prompt: What is the general relationship between a generative model's training data and the quality of what it can produce?

options.text: Output quality is strongly shaped by the breadth and quality of the training data
Training data has no effect on output
Only the amount of compute matters, never the data
Training data only matters for image models, never text

questions.explanation: A model reflects patterns in what it was trained on; gaps, biases or errors in that data tend to show up in its output.

questions.prompt: What risk does training data bias create for a generative AI application?

options.text: The model can produce outputs that unfairly favor or disadvantage certain groups
The model will always refuse to respond
The application automatically becomes non-compliant with all regulations

questions.explanation: If training data reflects historical or social biases, the model can reproduce or amplify them in its output unless this is specifically addressed.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud platform brings together tools to build, tune, deploy and manage generative AI models?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI is Google Cloud's unified machine learning platform, and it hosts the generative AI tooling including Model Garden and Gemini access.

questions.prompt: What is Gemini in the context of Google Cloud's generative AI offerings?

options.text: Google's family of multimodal foundation models

questions.explanation: Gemini is Google's family of large multimodal models, available through Vertex AI for building generative AI applications.

questions.prompt: What is Vertex AI Model Garden?

options.text: A curated catalog of foundation and open models a team can browse and deploy

questions.explanation: Model Garden lets teams discover, compare and deploy first-party, open-source and third-party models from one place in Vertex AI.

questions.prompt: What does 'grounding' a generative AI model's response mean on Google Cloud?

options.text: Connecting the model's output to a verifiable, current source of data such as Google Search or a company's own documents
Reducing the model's context window to zero

questions.explanation: Grounding ties generated answers to real, checkable sources, which reduces hallucination and lets the model reflect information beyond its training cutoff.

questions.prompt: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) add to a generative AI application?

options.text: It retrieves relevant documents at query time and feeds them to the model as context before it generates a response
It permanently retrains the model on every question asked
It removes the need for any prompt

questions.explanation: RAG looks up relevant information from a knowledge base at the moment of the query and includes it in the prompt, so the model answers with current, specific context.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud service is used to store embeddings and perform fast similarity search over them, a common building block for RAG?
questions.explanation: Vertex AI Vector Search indexes embeddings and finds the nearest matches quickly, which is what powers the retrieval step in a RAG pipeline.

questions.prompt: A team wants to add text-to-speech to an app without training any model. Which type of Google Cloud offering fits?
questions.explanation: Pre-built APIs (like Text-to-Speech, Translation and Vision) solve common tasks immediately, without any model training.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud product is purpose-built for creating conversational AI agents and chatbots?
questions.explanation: Google Cloud provides dedicated tooling (Dialogflow and Vertex AI Agent Builder) for building conversational agents, rather than building one from a raw model.

questions.prompt: Which type of Google Cloud model is used to generate new images from a text description?
questions.explanation: Imagen is Google's text-to-image generation model family, available through Vertex AI.

questions.prompt: Which Google Cloud offering assists developers by generating and explaining code using generative AI?
questions.explanation: Gemini Code Assist uses generative AI to suggest code, explain snippets and help developers move faster inside their IDE.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Vertex AI Studio?

options.text: A console for testing prompts, tuning parameters and comparing model responses interactively
A physical hardware store for GPUs

questions.explanation: Vertex AI Studio provides a UI to experiment with prompts and model settings before wiring a model into an application.

questions.prompt: After a generative AI model is tuned for a specific task, what does deploying it to a Vertex AI endpoint provide?

options.text: A way to serve predictions over an API for applications to call

questions.explanation: A Vertex AI endpoint exposes a deployed model as a callable API, so applications can request predictions from it in production.

questions.prompt: A support team wants answers grounded strictly in their own internal documentation, not the open internet. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Retrieval-augmented generation over their own document store
An ungrounded zero-shot prompt to a general model
A relational database with no AI component

questions.explanation: Grounding the model in the company's own documents through RAG keeps answers scoped to that content, rather than the model's general training data.

questions.prompt: A marketing team wants to generate several ad image variations from a text brief. Which Google Cloud capability is the direct fit?
questions.explanation: Imagen is designed specifically to turn a text description into generated images, which is exactly this use case.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of safety filters available in Vertex AI's generative AI tools?

options.text: Automatically flag or block outputs that fall into categories like hate speech or harassment

questions.explanation: Safety filters screen generated content against configurable harm categories, helping an application avoid surfacing unsafe output to users.

questions.prompt: A team wants a model that can accept an uploaded photo and answer questions about what is in it. Which capability do they need?

options.text: A multimodal model such as Gemini

questions.explanation: Multimodal models like Gemini can take image and text input together and reason across both in a single response.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of using an open model available through Model Garden instead of a proprietary API-only model?

options.text: It can typically be downloaded, inspected and self-hosted or fine-tuned with full control
It requires no infrastructure at all
It is always more accurate than any proprietary model
It removes the need for any evaluation

questions.explanation: Open models give teams more control over hosting, customization and inspection of the model, which proprietary API-only models do not offer.

questions.prompt: What is prompt engineering?

options.text: The practice of designing inputs to a model to reliably get a desired kind of output
Writing the model's underlying source code

questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is iterating on instructions, structure and examples in a prompt to steer a model's output without changing the model itself.

questions.prompt: Which change to a prompt most directly tends to reduce ambiguity in a model's response?

options.text: Being specific about the desired format, audience and constraints
Making the prompt as vague as possible
Asking multiple unrelated questions in one prompt

questions.explanation: A specific prompt that states the format, audience and constraints gives the model less room to guess what is actually wanted.

questions.prompt: What is chain-of-thought prompting?

options.text: Asking the model to reason step by step before giving a final answer
Chaining multiple unrelated models together randomly
A method for compressing a prompt to a single word

questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to show intermediate reasoning steps, which often improves accuracy on multi-step problems.

questions.prompt: Why is human evaluation still important even when a generative AI model can be tested automatically?

options.text: Automated metrics often miss nuance, tone and factual correctness that a human reviewer can catch
Automated evaluation is always more accurate
Human evaluation removes the need for any testing
It is required by every cloud provider's terms of service

questions.explanation: Automated scoring can measure some properties well, but subtleties like tone, correctness and appropriateness often still need a human judgment.

questions.prompt: When is fine-tuning generally a better choice than prompting alone?

options.text: When a task needs a consistent, specialized behavior that prompting cannot reliably achieve
When you want to change the model's behavior for a single one-off request
When you have no task-specific data available
Fine-tuning is always the better choice in every case

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is worth the extra effort and data requirement when a task needs durable, specialized behavior beyond what prompting alone can reliably deliver.

questions.prompt: How does grounding a model's response in a company's own data reduce hallucination?

options.text: It gives the model verified, relevant source material to base the answer on instead of relying purely on memorized patterns
It deletes the model's training data
It disables the model's ability to generate text
It has no effect on hallucination

questions.explanation: When the model is shown real source material at query time, it has something concrete to draw from rather than generating purely from what it memorized during training.

questions.prompt: Lowering a model's temperature setting for a customer-facing FAQ bot would most likely have which effect?

options.text: More consistent, predictable answers to similar questions

questions.explanation: A lower temperature reduces randomness in generation, which is usually desirable when consistency matters more than creative variety.

questions.prompt: What is a benefit of maintaining a golden dataset of example prompts and ideal responses for a generative AI application?

options.text: It provides a consistent benchmark for evaluating changes to the model or prompt over time
It replaces the need for any monitoring
It guarantees the model will never make mistakes
It is required to enable multimodal input

questions.explanation: A golden dataset gives a stable reference point, so a team can tell whether a prompt or model change actually improved quality rather than just guessing.

questions.prompt: A developer needs a model's response to reliably parse as JSON for downstream code. What is the most direct technique?

options.text: Explicitly instruct the model to output valid JSON in a defined schema, and validate the response
Hope the model happens to format it correctly

questions.explanation: Being explicit about the required structure, and validating the output before using it, is the reliable way to get machine-parseable responses.

questions.prompt: What is the typical relationship between prompt iteration and output quality?

options.text: Testing and refining a prompt against real examples usually improves output quality over the first draft
The first version of a prompt is always optimal
Iterating on a prompt has no effect on output
Prompt iteration only matters for image models

questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is iterative: testing against real examples and adjusting wording, structure or examples typically improves results over time.

questions.prompt: What is the general goal of a responsible AI framework in a generative AI deployment?

options.text: Ensuring AI systems are developed and used fairly, safely and transparently
Maximizing model size regardless of impact
Removing all human oversight from AI systems
Avoiding any documentation of how a model works

questions.explanation: Responsible AI frameworks set principles and practices for fairness, safety, privacy and transparency across the AI system's lifecycle.

questions.prompt: Why would an organization establish an AI governance review process before deploying a generative AI feature?

options.text: To assess risks like bias, privacy and compliance before the feature reaches users
To slow down every project for no reason
It is only relevant for image-generation products
To avoid ever measuring the feature's performance

questions.explanation: A governance review catches foreseeable risks, such as bias or data privacy issues, before they reach real users rather than after.

questions.prompt: What is a key data privacy consideration when feeding customer data into a generative AI model?

options.text: Ensuring the data is handled and used according to privacy commitments and regulations, including how it may or may not be used for training
There are no privacy considerations for AI systems
All customer data can be freely used to train any model
Privacy only matters for structured databases, not AI

questions.explanation: Feeding customer data into a model raises the same data-handling obligations as any other use, plus specific questions about whether it may be used for further training.

questions.prompt: Which is the most meaningful way to measure the business value of a generative AI initiative?

options.text: Tracking outcomes tied to business goals, such as time saved or conversion improvement, not just model accuracy
Counting the number of parameters in the model
Measuring only how large the training dataset was

questions.explanation: Business value comes from the outcome the AI enables (time saved, revenue, satisfaction), not from technical properties of the model itself.

questions.prompt: What is a common organizational risk when rolling out a generative AI tool to employees?

options.text: Employees using it without training on its limitations, leading to over-trusting incorrect output
Employees being unable to access the internet
The tool being too slow to ever be adopted
There being no organizational risk at all

questions.explanation: Without training on what the tool gets wrong, employees can treat confident-sounding, incorrect output as reliable, which is a real operational risk.

questions.prompt: When prioritizing generative AI use cases, which combination is generally the strongest starting point?

options.text: High business value and low risk, such as an internal drafting assistant with human review
High risk and low value use cases
Any use case, regardless of oversight
Only fully autonomous, unreviewed customer-facing decisions

questions.explanation: Starting with high-value, lower-risk use cases (especially ones with a human in the loop) builds experience and trust before tackling higher-stakes applications.

questions.prompt: Why should a business consider the source and licensing of training data used by a generative AI model it adopts?

options.text: Because it can affect intellectual property risk and the rights around content the model produces
Licensing has no bearing on generative AI
Only open-source models raise any IP questions
It only matters for image models

questions.explanation: How a model was trained, and under what license, can affect a business's legal exposure around the content it generates and uses.

questions.prompt: What is a sound first step for an organization building a generative AI strategy?

options.text: Identifying specific business problems the technology can address, rather than adopting it for its own sake
Deploying the largest available model everywhere immediately

questions.explanation: A strategy grounded in specific problems worth solving, rather than technology for its own sake, is what turns generative AI into a measurable business outcome.
